studiodudoublev.summary: Seasonal Italian gelato shop in Da'an; reviewers call it one of Taipei's best scoops, with flavours that change with the produce calendar.
highlights: Fruit flavours taste of the real ingredient; meringue bits at the bottom add texture
Seasonal and coffee collabs (e.g. with Simple Kaffa) are the most praised
Friendly, efficient staff even with a queue
lowlights: Pricey for gelato
Tiny space, mostly standing
Some regular fruit flavours run sweet; tasting samples no longer offered

celebread.acs.summary: Sourdough specialist off Anhe Road; open kitchen, one communal table, and loaves that regulars reorder weekly.
signature: Walnut / pecan-cranberry (核桃 / 胡桃蔓越莓)
highlights: Crisp crust, moist chewy open crumb, gentle sourness
Breads are cooled before slicing — reviewers appreciate the care
Reserve via LINE; popular flavours sell out
lowlights: Walk-ins often find little left
Some find the crust tough and the sourness strong for first-timers
Staff described as reserved

yu_chocolatier.summary: Chef Cheng Yu-hsuan's award-winning chocolatier-pâtisserie near the Ren'ai roundabout; often called Taiwan's best chocolate cake.
signature: Shibusa dark chocolate cake (澀井巧克力蛋糕)
Whisky / brandy bonbons (威士忌 / 白蘭地)
highlights: Deep, balanced chocolate with liqueur notes; mille-feuille assembled to order
Elegant, quiet dining room and knowledgeable service
Popular with Japanese and Korean visitors; good gift boxes
lowlights: NT$250 minimum spend and 90-minute limit for dine-in
Some fruit-forward cakes (e.g. kumquat jasmine) read as just sour
Hard to park; book on weekends

okashi_kau.summary: Japanese-style pâtisserie by baking teacher Lin Geng-chen near Songshan Cultural Park, also selling baking tools and ingredients.
highlights: Not too sweet, bright acidity, many-layered flavours
Excellent puff pastry — crisp, fragrant, not greasy
Minimum spend is one dessert (no drink required)
lowlights: Some find matcha flavours weak
No reservations; wait for seats on site
Short opening days (Thu–Sun)

heritagetaipei.summary: New American bakery-café in a restored camera-street shophouse near Ximen; the cinnamon roll is one of Taipei's most talked-about.
signature: Sea-salt devil's food cake (海鹽魔鬼蛋糕)
highlights: Generous American-style bakes; brunch and coffee too
Warm brick interior and attentive staff
Guava coffee is a signature drink
lowlights: Several desserts called too sweet
Busy weekends: book ahead, service can be stretched
NT$200 minimum + 10% service; cramped two-tops

minuit1200.summary: Late-night (4pm–midnight) French tart shop by Zhongxiao Fuxing, known for Taiwanese seasonal fruit tarts.
highlights: Crisp, praised tart shells and generous fruit
Open late — a rare after-dinner dessert option
Polite, patient staff (good with tourists)
lowlights: Expensive (NT$400–500+ per slice; slices are large)
Some complaints about chocolate tarts with soft shells
Hard to park

lilinli_tw.summary: Reservation-only dessert fine dining in Zhongshan: seasonal plated-dessert tasting menus mixing sweet and savoury Taiwanese ingredients.
highlights: Inventive pairings (bitter melon, eggplant, perilla, kombu) that still read as desserts
Chef Wise presents each course; warm service
Compared favourably with Bib Gourmand HUGH
lowlights: Very hard to book; menus sell out on release
High price (~NT$3,280 + 10%)
Occasional complaints about team attitude

patisseriecatherine2023.summary: Small Songshan pâtisserie famous for its 'shooting star' layered egg tarts, plus dacquoise and financiers for gifting.
signature: Vanilla 'shooting star' egg tart (流星蛋塔)
Bubble-tea pearl egg tart (啵啵珍珠)
highlights: Flaky, crackling layered crust with rich custard
Premium ingredients, not too sweet; good gift packaging
Phone ahead to reserve tarts
lowlights: Savoury flavours (e.g. basil pork) miss for some
Pop-up batches can be greasy
Mid-high price (~NT$130 per tart)

leavenworkshop.summary: Self-taught sourdough baker's tiny shop near Zhongshan; the Friday sourdough cinnamon rolls draw daily queues.
highlights: Scones praised as the best soft-style scones in town
Owner explains each bread and how to store it
Very open, crackling crust
lowlights: Long outdoor queue; items sell out before your turn
Cash only, no receipts, only two customers inside at once
Some loaves too dark/bitter and very thick-crusted

goldenrod_patisserie.summary: Bright, roomy café-pâtisserie tucked into a lane near Liuzhangli, a 'hidden gem' for refined, not-too-sweet cakes.
signature: Summer mango cheesecake tart (夏芒生乳酪)
highlights: Silky creams and well-balanced, adult sweetness
Plenty of seats and sockets; quiet even on weekends
Good specialty coffee
lowlights: Cash only
No table reservations (call to hold cakes)
One-drink minimum to dine in

renxren2.0.summary: Taipei outpost of a Taitung bakery-café with a calm, wood-toned Japanese-style room, known for its toast and bagels.
signature: Toast / thick toast (吐司 / 厚片)
Pesto chicken sandwich (青醬雞肉三明治)
highlights: Bagels with a wide sweet/savoury range; toast and sandwiches crisp and well-filled
Bright, quiet, cosy space smelling of coffee and bread
Pistachio and cream-cheese spreads and a not-too-sweet soy milk tea praised
lowlights: Some found it underwhelming vs. the hype; espresso drinks just average
Scones dry; bagels toasted firm and chewy
Popular sandwich fillings sell out by afternoon

goody_patisserie.summary: Weekend-only, takeaway-only French pâtisserie in a lane near Technology Building MRT, famed for cinnamon rolls and Saint-Honoré.
signature: Cinnamon roll / green Sichuan pepper roll (肉桂捲 / 青花椒肉桂捲)
Muscat white wine mousse (麝香白酒)
highlights: Canelé with shatteringly crisp shell and strong vanilla — a 'top canelé' for several
Silky mousses and moist sponges, rich but not cloying
Clear, transparent pre-order system and attentive owners
lowlights: Pre-order via weekly Wednesday menu; open Fri–Sun only, no dine-in or delivery
Refrigerated bakes can taste of the fridge; choux soften, cinnamon roll lacks fresh-baked aroma
Cinnamon roll glaze runs sweet for some

saintpaul_tw.summary: Hugely popular Yonghe neighbourhood bakery open till 10pm, with a wide range of breads, cakes and its famous QQ cakes.
signature: Saint Paul big bun / cheese Q-bing (聖保羅大餅 / 起司Q餅)
Dubai chocolate cake / Q-bing (杜拜巧克力)
highlights: Freshly baked, fragrant breads at modest prices
Creative seasonal cakes; online pre-order with store pick-up
Mostly very warm, friendly staff
lowlights: Pre-orders (e.g. Dubai Q-bing) can take about a week
Isolated reports of a rude staff member mishandling a cake pick-up
One regular felt cakes have become sweeter

thebakingmissruby.summary: Scone and soft-cookie specialist with branches at Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hall, Zhongshan and Nanjing Sanmin, plus gift boxes.
signature: Brown sugar soy-milk crunch scone (黑糖豆乳脆脆)
Hokkaido four-leaf cheesecake fat cookie (北海道四葉乳酪胖餅乾)
Lava dark cocoa fat cookie (誇張熔岩黑可可)
Raw chocolate marble (生巧克力大理石)
highlights: Big, thick soft cookies with crisp edges and rich fillings
Many flavours and nice gift-box packaging; pre-order online
Drink discount with a scone; cute takeaway glasses
lowlights: Scones can be dry and flavours not distinct; cookies pricey
Lava and dark-chocolate cookies very sweet/rich to finish alone
Branch inconsistency — weaker service and fillings reported at one store

terra_beantobar.summary: Bean-to-bar chocolate shop with Taiwan's widest range of origins, single-origin drinks and chocolate desserts in a plant-filled space.
signature: Single-origin hot / nitro chocolate (單品熱巧克力 / 氮氣冰巧克力)
'Around the world' chocolate tasting set (環遊世界巧克力片)
highlights: Origin-by-origin chocolate bars with free tastings and complimentary cacao beans
Friendly staff who explain the products
Elegant, green, open interior
lowlights: Few, uncomfortable seats (rough stone bar edges)
Everything is sweet; rich cakes best shared
Hot chocolate lacks depth for some; closed Wednesdays in Oct

bobonono.bakery.summary: Natural-ingredient bakery for gifting, best known for pound cakes, wedding cakes (喜餅) and baby full-month boxes; no additives.
signature: Pomelo baozhong tea ring pound cake (蜜柚包種圈圈)
Banana passion-fruit thin cookie (香蕉百香薄餅)
Plum purple-sweet-potato thin cookie (甘梅紫薯薄餅)
Chocolate corn-flake cookie (巧克力玉米脆片)
highlights: Local Taiwanese ingredients, no chemical additives, reduced sugar
Detailed, attentive tasting sessions for wedding and baby boxes
Moist pound cakes; eco-friendly yet attractive packaging
lowlights: Some pastries still on the sweet side
Order mix-up with a promised freebie, handled with blame on the customer

guyu.tw.summary: Japanese-style bakery-café on Keqiang Road in Tianmu with an open kitchen, known for its fleur de sel butter roll.
signature: Fleur de sel butter roll (鹽之花奶油捲)
highlights: Salt butter roll crisp outside, chewy inside, lightly salty
Calm Japanese interior with quality tableware; friendly staff
Creative fillings like miso butter roll
lowlights: Full by 10-something on weekends
Small selection; cinnamon flavour mild in the cinnamon roll

des_glaneuses.summary: Bakery and kitchen whose bread counter is praised as much as its weekend bistro set menus.
signature: Crisp classic croissant (原味脆皮可頌)
Ham and cheese bagel (火腿起司貝果)
highlights: Flaky, buttery laminated breads; crusty bâtards that reheat well
Quality ingredients and careful details in the cooking
Nicely designed packaging; bread bags folded neatly
lowlights: Bread is a bit pricey
Bistro dining is weekend-only by online booking; portions small for a 3-hour meal (older review)

lerubanpatisserie.summary: Chef Lee Yi-hsi's long-running single-shop French pâtisserie, famed for seasonal peach daifuku and gift boxes like egg-yolk pastries.
signature: Grandma's lemon cake (老奶奶檸檬蛋糕)
highlights: Refined, seasonal cakes using fresh local produce
Moist, bright lemon cake and classic French chocolate cake
Wide range of gift boxes, cookies and scones on site
lowlights: Many complaints about service and a poor in-store flow
Gift-box packaging and egg-yolk pastry quality seen as slipping
Weekend waits; seasonal items sell out in pre-order

drifter_dreamland.summary: Matcha-green, dinosaur-themed dessert shop open Fri–Sun, known for intense matcha cakes and drinks.
highlights: Rich, deep matcha flavour that isn't cloying
Thoughtful all-green décor; Wi-Fi and sockets
Friendly communication and careful delivery for whole cakes
lowlights: Few seats; fills up in the afternoon
One-drink minimum for dine-in; bookings open on the 15th for next month
Some items unavailable on the day; a bit pricey

crem_tw.summary: Cream-cake specialist (sister of 初衷小鹿) selling square mini cakes and 4–8" celebration cakes with a stylish accessory kit.
signature: Red oolong fig cake (紅烏龍無花果)
Narcissus oolong peach (水仙烏龍蜜桃)
highlights: Light cream that stays easy to eat; balanced tea-and-fruit pairings
Reusable steel cutlery, matchbox and candle kit add occasion
Cute, attentive staff; free tea while you wait
lowlights: Not cheap per cake
Cookie base is hard to cut and turns soggy
Weekend in-store items need Tuesday-night pre-order

brillante_patisserie.summary: Shilin pâtisserie on Wenlin Road selling French ice cream, cakes, viennoiserie and bread, listed among the '500 Sweets'.
highlights: Large, very flaky croissants that are good value
Elegant, not-too-sweet cakes; airy chocolate panettone
Friendly staff and thoughtful touches in the shop
lowlights: Sourdough judged dry and powdery
Some cakes taste only of sugar and are pricey
Very little seating; cakes can shift in takeaway boxes

feedthewife.summary: Cinnamon-roll, sourdough and American-dessert bakery in a lane by the Botanical Garden.
highlights: Soft, cinnamon-rich rolls with a tangy, not-too-sweet frosting
Carrot cake called the most authentic in Taiwan
Large, crisp croissants; clear reheating instructions
lowlights: Small daily quantities; reserve or come early
Cinnamon roll ~NT$140 felt pricey
Cash payment

petitchouxx18.summary: Two-person, reservation-only cake studio on the second floor of a Dadaocheng old house, focused on seasonal fruit cakes.
signature: Seasonal fruit cream cakes (季節水果蛋糕)
Pistachio cherry cocoa cake (開心果櫻桃可可)
highlights: Light, layered cream cakes that aren't too sweet
Quiet antique-filled shoes-off space for rare dine-in slots
Beautiful packaging and candles; reasonable prices
lowlights: Fully pre-order; cake days limited and posted on IG
Pick-up by ringing a doorbell per ordering rules

engawa_cake.summary: Takeaway-focused cake studio in a house near Houshanpi MRT, selling daily slices plus whole cakes; garden is photogenic.
signature: Peach cream cake (水蜜桃奶油蛋糕)
highlights: Fresh fruit and airy, not-greasy cream
Pudding with deep egg flavour and bittersweet caramel
Friendly staff who explain each flavour
lowlights: Dine-in only two tables at set slots — must book
No toilet on site
Pudding NT$150; mille crêpe fruit can be sour

yi.ke.song.summary: Croissant shop on Jinzhou Street (near Zhongshan Junior High MRT) with a Songjiang branch, filling croissants with Taiwanese flavours.
signature: Jin Xuan tea cream croissant (金萱清茶生乳)
highlights: Inventive sweet and savoury fillings, generously filled
Crisp outside, soft and chewy inside — good even chilled
Frequent buy-5-get-1 deals; friendly owner
lowlights: Unit prices on the high side (~NT$65–86 filled)
Some flavours (e.g. apple cheese) smaller and flatter

yangtai2020.summary: Pre-order-only cake studio now based inside 點冰室 near Jiancheng Park, known for Taiwanese-ingredient cakes and pretty wrapping.
signature: Licorice guava Basque cheesecake (甘草芭樂巴斯克)
highlights: Distinctive Taiwanese flavours, e.g. star anise and coriander-peanut
Beautiful cloth-wrapped packaging; easy IG ordering
Kind, gracious owner
lowlights: Now pre-order only — no dine-in or walk-in; whole cakes 5 days ahead
Pick-up 14:00–18:00; fully booked dates posted on IG Stories
Basque base itself called a bit plain

quelques_p.summary: Chef Lai's takeaway French pâtisserie in an East District lane off Ren'ai Road, one of Taipei's best-known for Saint-Honoré.
signature: Honey whisky cheesecake (蜂蜜威士忌起司蛋糕)
Tieguanyin chocolate tart (鐵觀音巧克力塔)
highlights: Vanilla-flecked Chantilly that is light, not greasy; crisp caramel choux
Fine, layered textures across the range
Careful takeaway packing with ice packs
lowlights: No dine-in now — choux may soften on the way home
Pricey (Saint-Honoré ~NT$320); some find cream ratio too high
Pre-order and pay in advance; walk-in selection incomplete

lune_dessert.summary: Dog café-dessert shop in Sanchong near St. Ignatius High School MRT, with resident huskies and a Samoyed and semi-baked Basque cheesecakes.
signature: Pistachio Basque with mango (開心果巴斯克+芒果)
highlights: Gentle, cute resident dogs; space stays odour-free
Creamy, soft-centred Basques; boozy grown-up tiramisu
Patient owner happy to customise orders
lowlights: Few seats: book ahead, table held only 10 min, 90-min limit, one-drink minimum
No pets or under-12s
Drinks served in tall-bottomed cups feel small

mosaicpastryshop.summary: Tianmu canelé specialist billed as the 'ceiling of canelés', with many filled flavours and pop-up counters (e.g. Taipei Main Station).
highlights: Caramelised crisp shell, moist chewy centre; many rotating flavours
Freezes well — thaw 15 min; elegant 1/4/9-piece gift boxes
Fillings not overly sweet for most
lowlights: Some find shells thick, hard and sticky, and fillings too sweet
Takeaway only, no seating
A report of pressuring counter staff at the Tianmu shop

cone20190222.summary: Japanese-craft cake shop in Minsheng Community using seasonal Taiwanese fruit, popular for 4-inch birthday cakes.
signature: Pistachio caramel apple (開心果焦糖蘋果)
Strawberry cream cake (草莓奶油蛋糕)
Dark chocolate cherry (黑巧克力櫻桃)
highlights: Light, not-cloying cream and soft, moist sponge; quality ingredients
Flavours rotate with the season; 4-inch sizes available
Kind owners; slice boxes have internal supports
lowlights: No dine-in, and nowhere nearby to eat
Not cheap
Pistachio-caramel apple reads bitter to kids

la.grotta.cafe.summary: 'Little cave' café-pâtisserie near Ximen (Exit 2) open late, with a daily-changing dessert line-up posted on IG at 10am.
signature: Matcha lavender mille-feuille (抹茶薰衣草千層)
Coffee hazelnut Basque (咖啡榛果巴斯克)
Murcott iced coffee (茂谷柑冰咖啡)
highlights: Creative, ever-changing desserts; mille-feuille called Taipei's best
Tea lattes and fruit-tea/coffee drinks also strong
Relaxed room with floor-to-ceiling windows; open to 22:00
lowlights: One-drink minimum; weekends no booking, 2-hour limit
Some drinks unremarkable; Basque can get cloying
Not suited to working; closed Thursdays

albuca_dessert.summary: Da'an pâtisserie with shops on Taishun and Tong'an streets, known for dacquoise and baked-goods gift boxes with pretty wrapping.
signature: Caramel cheddar dacquoise (焦糖切達起司)
Jin Xuan fig financier (金萱無花果費南雪)
highlights: Crisp-shelled, soft-filled dacquoise, sweet but not cloying
Thoughtful gift boxes with selectable wrapping and plant-tied bags
Owner keeps developing new flavours
lowlights: Flavour availability varies by day
Some cakes (e.g. charlotte) rich and heavy
Closed Mondays

sugarspicetw.summary: Taipei Dunnan flagship of the Taichung-born confectioner, the go-to shop for Taiwanese nougat and gift boxes.
signature: Dubai chocolate mochi (杜拜巧克力Q餅)
highlights: Nougat praised as not too sweet and not sticky
Classic souvenir stop; staff friendly and helpful with gift orders
New items (cookies, Dubai chocolate mochi) keep regulars coming back
lowlights: Dubai chocolate mochi small and a bit greasy for the price
More a gift shop than a café — little to eat on site

myradessertlab.summary: Dacquoise and warm-cookie specialist by the park off Yongkang Street, blending Taiwanese flavours with French technique; currently closed while relocating.
signature: Fleur de sel butter red bean dacquoise (鹽花奶油紅豆)
Mian-cha black sesame warabi mochi (麵茶黑芝麻蕨餅)
Double-tea mochi soft cookie (雙茶麻糬軟餅乾)
highlights: Chilled dacquoise with silky, intense fillings and crisp-light shells, not too sweet
Friendly, unpressured service and detailed explanations
Handsome gift boxes; no minimum spend
lowlights: Pricey at ~NT$120 each; eat within two hours of leaving the fridge
Warm cookies called inconsistent in texture; some packets poorly sealed
Temporarily closed — new location pending

humanity__sweets.summary: Tiny cream-puff shop opposite NTU in Gongguan, billed as the original bubble-tea cream puff and 2026 Taiwan Cream Puff Festival favourite.
signature: Bubble milk tea cream puff (珍珠鮮奶茶泡芙)
Chocolate ice cream puff (巧克力冰淇淋泡芙)
Tiramisu cream puff (提拉米蘇泡芙)
highlights: Unusually crisp, caramelised shells that don't go soggy
Many flavours with generous, not-cloying fillings; house-made ice cream
Polite staff explain how to eat them; free delivery for big orders
lowlights: Prices high for fairly small puffs
Pearls in the bubble-tea puff too soft; milk-tea filling sweet for some

frenchtwist_bakery.summary: New Aussie-meets-French bakery and brunch spot in Minsheng Community with a bright, upscale room and twice-daily bakes.
signature: Matcha mochi bow croissant (抹茶麻糬蝴蝶結可頌)
Strawberry matcha cloud latte (草莓抹茶雲朵拿鐵)
highlights: Very buttery, crisp croissants compared to Paris
Bright, modern, spacious interior with thoughtful touches
Smiling, helpful staff
lowlights: Expensive: croissants NT$150–195, breakfast tower NT$1,080, plus service charge
Brunch looks better than it tastes (hard butter, hard bread); matcha latte poor
Limited tables — weekend mornings can fill up

libreadry.summary: Famous queue-worthy bakery at Zhongxiao Dunhua MRT Exit 3, known for mentaiko baguette and egg tarts across a huge range.
signature: Mille-feuille / layered egg tart (千層蛋塔)
highlights: Mentaiko bread generously spread, balanced salty-spicy, tasty even cold
Huge variety of European and Japanese breads, frequently restocked
Free water and tea for the queue; friendly staff and bakers
lowlights: Queues of 10–20 min; crowded, narrow aisles
Mentaiko limited to 6 per person and gets oily once cold
Some fancy items pricey (~NT$220) or hard and chewy

kokowalker_cake.summary: Japanese-style pâtisserie in Xindian (near Xindian District Office MRT Exit 1) known for low-sugar chiffon cakes and Basque cheesecakes.
signature: Fruit cream chiffon cake (水果奶油戚風)
highlights: Low-sugar, light cream that even older relatives enjoy
Fresh, plentiful fruit and creative seasonal flavours
Cosy, homely space; good coffee
lowlights: Whole cakes pricey (e.g. 7" fruit chiffon NT$2,300); fruit 'extra' felt light
Counter service felt cold to some
Limited seats, no table reservations; cake orders by LINE/phone only

peacepiece_bakery.summary: Warm, Japanese-feeling neighbourhood bakery-café in a quiet residential corner, open Fri–Mon, with a popular bread platter.
signature: Bread platter with olive oil and jam (麵包盤)
Yuzu-pepper bacon bread (柚子胡椒培根)
highlights: Chewy, crusty breads with beautiful open crumb
Generous bread platter is a filling meal for two
Smiling owner; cosy room with cute details
lowlights: Cash or bank transfer only
One-drink minimum and drinks are ordinary; no table bookings
Some loaves baked to the point of burnt

boulangerie_ours.summary: Low-key bakery-café known for sourdough, cinnamon rolls and croissants, with a cosy dine-in space and sandwiches until 15:00.
signature: Cinnamon roll / cinnamon roll croissant (肉桂捲)
highlights: Chewy, balanced sourdough and very flaky apple pastry
Dense, springy cinnamon roll; not overly sweet
Clean, relaxing space; staff explain the foreign-only labels
lowlights: Popular items sell out — reserve ahead; closes early when sold out
Coffee au lait ordinary; sandwiches take ~10 min and can be oily
Hojicha croissant flavour faint

envie0520.summary: Small Zhongshan French pâtisserie near Zhongshan Elementary MRT, best known for Saint-Honoré, with a list of Taiwanese craft gins.
highlights: Fine, layered Saint-Honoré with crisp chilled choux
Can reserve tables; also on Uber Eats
Wide drink list incl. ~14 Taiwanese-ingredient gins
lowlights: Pricey (Saint-Honoré NT$320, 6" NT$1,350); NT$200 minimum, 90-min limit
Several find caramel + custard too sweet and heavy
Only ~3–4 tables; hard parking; closed Wednesdays

byron__huang.summary: Pre-order-only egg-yolk pastry (蛋黃酥) maker whose version has a crisp caramel-cookie base; also does cakes and fruit jars.
signature: Strawberry cream cake with pudding (草莓布丁蛋糕)
highlights: Crisp, toasty caramel cookie base adds texture and aroma
Smooth, not-too-sweet red bean with salted yolk
Cakes partly customisable; owner's craftsmanship praised
lowlights: Sells out — November fully booked, no walk-in sales; pick-up 17:00–19:00
Minimum 6-piece box (NT$570, ~NT$90 each); yolk can be dry
Strict ordering rules (unpaid orders cancelled)

chochoco_chocolate.summary: Chocolate shop and French-style wedding-cookie (喜餅) brand with a Da'an showroom and Taichung branches.
signature: Wedding cookie gift boxes (喜餅禮盒)
highlights: Rich chocolate that is smooth and not overly sweet
Patient, professional staff run relaxed tasting sessions with tea
Stylish packaging and a designed showroom
lowlights: Most pieces are only one bite in size
Reviews skew to wedding tastings — less on everyday buying

nicecreamtaipei.summary: Flagship of a plant-based Italian gelato chain (7 shops) in the East District, famed for soy milk gelato and egg waffles.
highlights: Creamy plant-milk bases; real fruit flavours with no artificial taste
Free tastings and warm, cheerful staff
Fun upside-down cone presentation; bright, clean shop
lowlights: All-flavours cup pricey for the portion; flavours blur as it melts
Matcha egg waffle tasted off to one reviewer
Daily flavour selection can feel limited

5.tung_.summary: Mille-feuille specialist now near Liuzhangli MRT in a bigger, prettier space, also known for egg tarts and caramel pudding.
signature: Egg tarts incl. Dubai pistachio (蛋塔)
Hojicha cream / Marukyu Koyamaen (焙茶生乳)
highlights: Very crisp, distinct layers with two paired creams per flavour
Creams smooth and true to flavour (strong hojicha, real strawberry)
Seasonal specials like peach season and Mid-Autumn egg tarts
lowlights: Pastry can be too hard to cut and feels heavy
One-drink minimum to dine in and drinks are weak; pricey (~NT$260)
Popular items sell out; seasonal fruit quality inconsistent

petit_sam_liu.summary: 'Little Sam' canelé specialist selling via NOR.coffee and pop-ups, called the 'ceiling of canelés' for crisp shells and chilled fillings.
highlights: Extremely crisp shells with rich, cold centres; not too sweet
Premium ingredients; strong tea flavours
Friendly owner; good gift boxes
lowlights: Pistachio soft-serve cup NT$180 came with a burnt canelé
Canelés hard straight from the fridge — let them thaw
Location has moved between shop, pop-ups and partner café

senye_breadcoffee.summary: Bakery-café by Zhongxiao Fuxing MRT Exit 1 from the team behind 深夜裡的法國手工甜點, using Isigny butter in a dark-wood room.
highlights: Large, flaky, fresh croissants
Cosy wood-and-low-light atmosphere; friendly staff
Savoury pies and Basque cheesecake well liked
lowlights: Few seats; weekend waits
Not cheap; savoury pies small
Coffee hit-or-miss; no reheating for dine-in bread; salt roll dry

ppmillecrepes.summary: Bright, roomy mille-crêpe cake café with pop-up counters, popular for matcha, sesame and Earl Grey crêpe cakes.
signature: Black sesame mille crêpe (芝麻千層)
Earl Grey mille crêpe (伯爵千層)
highlights: Soft cake layers with fresh fruit; not too sweet for many
Bright, spacious, pretty interior
Fast turnaround on orders
lowlights: Cream can taste bland or greasy; some crêpe layers dry or missing cream
Dubai crêpe cake (NT$260) disappointed
Staff described as unfriendly; small tables, plastic cups

habitat311.summary: Minimalist dessert café on Songlong Road in Xinyi selling whole chiffon cakes, macarons and creative drinks.
signature: Whole chiffon cakes (整模戚風蛋糕)
highlights: Balanced, not-too-sweet desserts with good fruit-and-cream pairings
Calm, simple, elegant space
Regular new items; drinks also distinctive
lowlights: Whole-cake orders open on the 20th for the next month
Closed Mon–Tue in November; ordering via LINE only

risebakery.taipei.summary: Signless bakery on Xinyi Road near Xinyi Anhe MRT, now open one day a week, famed for its scones and cinnamon rolls.
highlights: Buttery, crumbly-crisp scones with moist centres
Well-balanced sourdough with good chew and clean sourness
Flaky croissants
lowlights: Open one day a week; walk-ins find little left — pre-order
Cash only; chaotic queue and checkout at peak
Cinnamon roll very sweet; focaccia oily

22dessert_studio.summary: Pre-order cream-roll and crispy-choux shop hidden in a Shida Road lane; takeaway only, no seating.
signature: Earl Grey cream roll (伯爵茶生乳捲)
Dubai chocolate Q-bing (杜拜巧克力Q餅)
highlights: Very crisp choux with pure, not-sweet fillings
Dubai Q-bing chewy, nutty and only lightly sweet
Moist cream rolls; nice leather-tied boxes
lowlights: Pre-order recommended; walk-in stock only at times posted on IG
No seating; popular items sell out

kang.artisanbakery.summary: Songshan artisan bakery (near Taipei Arena) open Tue–Sat, praised for crisp croissants that stay crunchy hours later.
signature: Truffle salt butter roll (松露鹽花奶油捲)
Little crown cinnamon (小小皇冠肉桂)
highlights: Croissants stay crisp even two hours after takeaway; not greasy
Fair prices vs. other famous bakeries
Staff bag items for you; pre-orders accepted
lowlights: Butter aroma lighter than some expect
Salt butter rolls, taro bun and apple tart only average for some
Parking inconvenient

eat.do.nut.summary: Croissant and fresh-donut stand from the 宜可頌 team, in the plaza behind McDonald's on Changchun Road, Zhongshan.
signature: Dubai chocolate donut (杜拜巧克力甜甜圈)
highlights: Fluffy donuts and crisp, not-too-sweet croissants
Friendly owners; tastings offered
lowlights: Some fillings bland or odd; plain custard in every donut
A bit pricey; apparently cash only
Short wait when someone ahead buys a lot

kitoya_cake.summary: Tucheng (New Taipei) cake studio since 2021 focused on pre-ordered whole cakes, with occasional bookable dine-in days for its parfaits.
signature: Muscat grape hojicha chiffon (麝香葡萄焙茶戚風)
highlights: Light, non-greasy cream and fresh Japanese fruit
Artful parfaits finishing with a low-sugar tea jelly
Beautiful Japanese-style space; friendly owner
lowlights: Whole cakes by reservation only, no stock; strict 30-min pick-up windows
Chiffon can be dry and firm; priced on the high side
Dine-in only a few days a month; closed Tue–Wed

rollbakery.summary: Banqiao branch of a known Taichung dessert shop, famed for cute animal-shaped cream dorayaki in gift boxes.
signature: Strawberry cream dorayaki (莓好生乳銅鑼燒)
Bean-paste pastry gift box (烏日餅 / 金旺餅)
highlights: Eat frozen like ice cream or thawed like cream cake
Reduced-sugar, not cloying fillings
Adorable designs great for gifting and kids; frequent promotions
lowlights: Keep frozen — best eaten soon after thawing
Reviews are mostly gifting-focused; little on everyday bakes

chuan_tung.summary: 40-year-old Tianmu bakery (three shops), now refurbished with cakes and French pastries, famed for its taro 'treasure box' cakes.
highlights: Chunky taro paste that older family members love
Bright, jewellery-shop-like store with attentive explanations
Good classic breads like coffee walnut toast
lowlights: Long-time fans say the taro roll recipe has changed for the worse
French-style pastries and pop-up cakes judged too sweet or coarse for the price
Popular items sell out by mid-afternoon

chillsoul7.summary: Small, laid-back bakery-café making wild-yeast sourdough, croissants, European and Japanese breads, and catering boxes.
signature: Scones incl. ruby black tea (司康)
Pesto chicken meatball croissant (青醬雞肉丸可頌)
highlights: Fresh, varied bakes with distinctive savoury breads
Very warm owner who explains items; dine-in bread reheated
Good value (three breads + Americano NT$230)
lowlights: Queues before opening; little left later — reserve via IG DM
Small shop

yoyu_bakerykitchen.summary: Husband-and-wife bread-and-cooking spot in Xinzhuang serving bread platters with stews and curries plus low-fat/sugar European breads.
signature: Red wine beef stew with bread (紅酒燉牛肉)
highlights: Tender, deeply flavoured stews and curries with non-greasy, crusty breads
Rich caramel pudding is a must-order
Warm owners who check you're full
lowlights: Only ~8 seats and two staff — queue before opening
Cash only; no toilet; weak air-con
Bread for takeaway only from 16:45

cocobrowniestaipei.summary: Brownie specialist with branches in Gongguan, Taipei Dome and Dongmen, also serving pound cakes, scones, coffee and wine.
signature: Cinnamon crumble pound cake (肉桂奶酥磅蛋糕)
Taiwan oolong gift box (台灣烏龍禮盒)
highlights: Many brownie flavours plus a wide dessert counter
Dim, cosy atmosphere; patient, friendly staff
Pound cakes and soft cookies not overly sweet
lowlights: Brownies too sweet for some
One-drink minimum to dine in
Can feel crowded when busy

voilab.lab.summary: French pâtisserie known for its 'jewel box' double-filled, four-tier dacquoise, with tea and matcha series and online ordering.
signature: Matcha orange liqueur dacquoise (抹茶香橘奶酒)
Passion-fruit mango Basque (百香芒果巴斯克)
highlights: Art-piece-like presentation and careful packaging
Bitter matcha cream balances sweet fillings
Friendly service
lowlights: High prices; some find shells dry and fillings too heavy
Cakes (e.g. Basque, Saint-Honoré) run too sweet
Not set up for dine-in; order online 2 days ahead; closed Sun–Mon

fluegelstudio.summary: Homemade-cake café near Taipower Building MRT Exit 2, a long-time favourite for big, generous European-style cakes.
signature: Rum chestnut Basque (萊姆酒栗子巴斯克)
Truffle chocolate grape (松露巧克力葡萄)
Caramel walnut cake (焦糖核桃白帽子)
highlights: Wide, high-quality cake range in generous slices
Relaxing wood-and-rattan space with natural light
Friendly staff who explain each cake
lowlights: Weekend waits (~30 min); cakes limited and sell out
Some cakes very sweet or large; lemon cake too sour
One-drink minimum; drinks average; opens 14:00 weekdays

kakigori_fumoto.summary: Pet-friendly Japanese kakigori shop in Sanchong with a resident cat, also serving Basque cake, pour-over and Oyaizu matcha.
signature: Matcha red bean kakigori (抹茶紅豆冰)
Japanese caramel pudding (日式焦糖布丁)
Oolong osmanthus mango ice (烏龍桂花芒果)
highlights: Snow-fine ice that melts instantly; balanced sweetness
Calm Japanese décor and a friendly owner (and cat)
Small/large sizes make it easy to try several
lowlights: Some bites are plain ice — toppings/sauce sparse
Cash only; ~NT$230–240 per bowl; one-item minimum
No reservations; slow as one person makes everything

heureuxvegan.summary: Vegan light-meal and dessert spot in Tianmu, now mainly a studio for catering, candy bars and wedding/baby gift boxes.
signature: Japanese vegan hamburg steak (日式漢堡排)
highlights: Inventive, juicy plant-based dishes that convert non-vegans
Rich, tea-heavy madeleines warmed for dine-in
Bright, cute, family- and baby-friendly space
lowlights: Shop now by appointment; mainly a catering/custom studio
Everything made to order — allow extra time

missvbakery.summary: Chifeng Street bakery-café in an old house (with a Dunbei branch), famous for its champion cinnamon rolls and brunch.
signature: Champion caramel sticky bun (冠軍焦糖黏黏包)
Cream cheese cinnamon roll (奶油起司肉桂捲)
highlights: Moist, layered rolls with gentle, balanced cinnamon
Soft scrambled eggs and well-composed brunch plates
Bright terrazzo-and-wood room popular with visitors
lowlights: Prices on the high side
Plain roll bland and dough a little sticky
Drinks and coffee only so-so; sous-vide chicken salty

dondonstudio.summary: Late-opening dessert studio pairing tea, cocktails and plated cakes in a dark, intimate room; book and reserve desserts ahead.
signature: Gardenia oolong cream cold brew (梔子烏龍奶霜冰滴)
highlights: Tea-led cakes where floral notes stay subtle; light creams
Creative drinks and cocktails; open late on weekends
Friendly solo owner; Google booking
lowlights: Very few seats — book and pre-reserve cakes or they sell out
Cakes large and rich for one person
Dine-in paused around Mid-Autumn gift-box season

deerdaytw.summary: Hidden Xinyi cake studio (since 2017, ~15–20 min walk from Xiangshan MRT) known for tea and fruit chiffon cakes.
signature: Shimen Tieguanyin chiffon (鐵觀音茶戚風)
Strawberry pistachio chiffon (草莓開心果戚風)
Strawberry cocoa chiffon (草莓可可戚風)
Lemon genmaicha chiffon (檸檬玄米茶戚風)
Strawberry custard roll (草莓卡士達蛋糕卷)
highlights: Strong tea flavour and soft, moist chiffon
Quality ingredients; fillings not overly sweet
Thoughtful details like contoured cake boards
lowlights: Whole cakes pre-order only; slices just on some weekends, announced day before
Only four tables; prices a bit high
Caramel sea-salt chiffon called far too sweet

enchantee.wedding.summary: French-style wedding-cookie (喜餅) brand by Zhongxiao Xinsheng MRT, with design-award-winning gift boxes and baby-month boxes.
signature: Chocolate fleur de sel cookie (巧克力鹽之花)
highlights: Cookies and cakes not too sweet, with clear flavours
Detailed, no-pressure tasting sessions
Handsome boxes and sturdy bags; good value
lowlights: Tasting by appointment; reviews centre on wedding/baby orders

ciaociaogoodfood.summary: Scone specialist with branches around Taipei (Dihua Street flagship, Yongkang, Hangzhou S. Rd.); a calm, roomy spot for scones and coffee.
signature: Toffee sea-salt scone (太妃海鹽司康)
Pudding with olive-oil ice cream (布丁冰淇淋)
Hojicha red-bean mochi (焙茶紅豆麻糬)
highlights: Crisp outside, moist inside scones in many flavours, not too sweet
Spacious, quiet room that fits the Dadaocheng old-street vibe
Pudding + ice cream combo is a sleeper hit
lowlights: One-drink minimum and 90-minute limit
Some drinks weak (e.g. matcha latte milky)
A few items run sweet

supranormalbc.summary: Tianmu bakery-café (also in Ruiguang) with an open kitchen, known for croissants, egg tarts and creative brunch.
signature: Watermelon juice / strawberry watermelon cake (西瓜)
Brown sugar cinnamon roll (黑糖肉桂捲)
Spicy shrimp scrambled egg croissant (熱辣蝦仁炒蛋可頌)
highlights: Super-flaky croissants and standout egg tarts
Carefully made brunch (real-tomato beans, crisp maple bacon, soft eggs)
Stylish glass open kitchen; friendly service
lowlights: Pricey
Small, cramped seating, loud music; no reservations
Drinks ordinary; menu translation errors

unpetitpeu_sucre.summary: Order-only French dessert studio near Yuanshan Station (Datong), known for canelés, hazelnut snacks and custom cakes.
signature: Caramel hazelnut bites (焦糖榛果寶寶)
Custom birthday cake with pudding (客製生日蛋糕)
highlights: Canelés crisp outside, custardy inside; hazelnut bites are addictive
Not too sweet; cream light and not greasy
Careful gift packaging and well-padded shipping; custom designs via IG
lowlights: Reservation-only, no dine-in; next month's cakes open on the 15th
Order via IG DM; several closure days a month
Canelés must be kept frozen or they go soft

mupatisserie.tw.summary: Two-storey French pâtisserie in a Muzha residential lane, with a European cottage interior and semi-outdoor garden upstairs.
highlights: Huge range; caramelised, crisp canelés and silky crêpe cakes
Tea-based cakes and light cream are not too sweet
Pretty space and a garden terrace; pet-friendly
lowlights: Pistachio items taste more of almond; daifuku hide sponge cake
NT$250 min, 90-min limit when full; drinks only americano or latte
Upstairs terrace gets hot with mosquitoes; past service complaints

but.we.love.butter.summary: Upscale butter-cookie brand with a theatrical shop near Songshan Airport, best known for its wedding-cookie gift boxes.
signature: Caramel salted-egg-yolk walnut (焦糖鹹蛋黃核桃)
highlights: Rich, pure buttery cookies; generous tasting samples
Complimentary tea and snack in a surreal, design-led space
Many stylish packaging options for gifting
lowlights: Pricey; service called correct but cold
Mixed boxes don't label flavours; mirror-shiny packaging
Popular flavours sell out; confusing entrance

rollingeyes_9.summary: Relaxed couple-run bakery-café off Dunhua South Road in Da'an, loved for cinnamon rolls, toast and inventive breads.
highlights: Watch the owner bake and eat bread fresh from the oven
Black tea bâtard tastes like bubble tea, no fake Earl Grey aroma
Warm, cheerful owners; easy pre-orders via IG/LINE
lowlights: Popular items sell out; baguette by pre-order only; closes early when sold out
One reviewer felt rushed and found the cinnamon roll dry, few walnuts
Hot cocoa too sweet

comfortzone.tw.summary: Cosy lane café near Liuzhangli Station known for fruit crêpe cakes, chiffons and warm cream-filled crêpes.
signature: Red guava lemon crêpe cake (紅心芭樂檸檬千層)
Cream crêpe with milk ice cream (奶油薄餅)
Pistachio Basque cheesecake (開心果巴斯克)
highlights: Fragrant crêpe layers with well-balanced cream, not cloying
Warm crêpes with ice cream and caramel apple are a hit
Good drinks (latte, brown sugar coffee, matcha coconut)
lowlights: Cash or transfer only; one-drink minimum and 90-min limit when full
Upstairs is small, tight and echoey
Some found service cold; no ice packs for takeaway

egghost_dessert.summary: Cat-café-style dessert shop on Sanyuan Street near Nanjichang Night Market, famous for chiffon cakes and open late.
signature: Matcha pudding chiffon (小山園抹茶布丁戚風)
Sesame crunch chiffon (濃芝麻脆脆戚風)
highlights: Resident shop cats and a homey, stylish two-floor space
Grown-up bitter matcha balances the sweet chiffon
Open until 11pm on weekends; sockets for laptops
lowlights: Drinks pricey (NT$160+) and small
Min one food + one drink, 2-hour limit; order and pay cash first
Some find food average and staff noisy

wuniquetaipei.summary: Small, hard-to-find Zhongshan (Nanxi) takeaway outpost of WUnique Pâtisserie, centred on its Saint-Honoré.
signature: Yang Zhi Gan Lu mango-pomelo cake (楊枝甘露)
Pink Lady rose-cranberry mousse (紅粉佳人)
highlights: Glossy caramel-shell choux and rich vanilla cream
Drink-inspired and floral petit gâteaux are refined and fresh
Ice packs included; LINE Pay accepted
lowlights: Entrance easy to miss; staff sometimes not yet in
Saint-Honoré called soft, less cohesive than at the old flagship
Takeaway only; one cake arrived watery

deuxdouxcremerie.summary: Ice-cream pâtisserie and sister shop of gelato maker Double-V, building parfaits and plated desserts from house ice creams.
signature: Mango coconut parfait (芒果椰奶芭菲)
Ice-cream dacquoise (冰淇淋夾心達克瓦茲)
highlights: Desserts look like artworks, with layered, natural flavours
Simple Kaffa coffee; free unsweetened tea
Price matched by quality ingredients
lowlights: NT$300 minimum + 10% service, 90-minute limit
Tiny, crowded space with no air-conditioning
Some flavours too boozy

milesqcafe.summary: White minimalist Xinyi shop near the World Trade Center making French-style roll cakes and custom celebration cakes.
signature: French chocolate ganache roll (法式生巧)
highlights: Moist sponge, fresh light cream; matcha roll is properly bitter
Low NT$100 minimum and flexible ordering
Friendly, courteous owners
lowlights: Cash or transfer only
Only ~8 seats; dine-in on weekends only
Chocolate roll disappointed some for the price

purebreadbakery.summary: East District sourdough bakery with seating, known for cinnamon rolls, jalapeño loaves and wide range of European breads.
highlights: Honest ingredients and no commercial-yeast taste
Many sourdoughs, croissants and mini quiches; frozen tiramisu loved
Careful packing for delivery
lowlights: Order online 3 days ahead; no in-store holds
Some breads dry, very hard; fig filling sparse
Slicing not always available; staff a common complaint

hoganbakery.summary: Huge natural-starter bakery at Global Mall Banqiao with 140+ breads; known for its champion wine-longan loaf.
signature: Wine longan walnut bread (酒釀桂圓)
highlights: Enormous, constantly restocked selection plus cookies and jams
Chewy European breads with walnuts, fruit and wine aromas
Cheerful morning staff; fresh salads and coffee
lowlights: Long-time fans report decline (canelé no longer crisp)
Some find breads look better than they taste
Complaint of regulars being served first

savoeur_glacerie.summary: Taoyuan-born French ice-cream shop now in a Bade Road lane (Songshan), with rotating tea and seasonal flavours.
highlights: Tea flavours intense, with a high ratio of tea leaves
Pure, clean flavours and decent portions
Friendly staff; generous tastings
lowlights: Only a couple of seats plus a standing table
Flavours rotate; favourites may be seasonal or gone
Some say complaints raised months ago went unaddressed

xiong_hojia.summary: Banqiao egg-cake stall (10 min from Fuzhong Station) by a former dental assistant, selling bichon-dog-shaped waffles.
highlights: Crisp shell, soft inside, strong egg aroma
Generous fillings; the cheese stretches
Warm, dedicated owner; loyalty card
lowlights: Afternoon/evening hours only (from 3pm weekdays)
Pre-order via LINE to avoid waiting
Monthly closures announced on IG

kawa_patisserie.summary: Family-oriented cake brand from Zhonghe/Yonghe (Yongyuan Road branch), popular for strawberry and ice-cream birthday cakes.
signature: Watermelon mango ice-cream cake (西瓜芒果冰淇淋蛋糕)
Strawberry Calpis cake (草莓可爾必思)
highlights: Not too sweet, light cream, generous fruit
Many cute cakes designed for children
Kind, patient staff who add party extras
lowlights: Cash and Taiwan Pay only
Box and packaging hard to open
Best ordered ahead for pick-up

flourishbakery2018.summary: Bakery-café opposite a park near Jiangzicui Station, using quality eggs and butter; known for its strawberry cream bun.
highlights: Unique fillings, not overly sweet; biscuits praised
Bright space with big windows facing the park
Friendly owner and staff; LINE Pay
lowlights: Queues; strawberry bun limited to two per person
Some breads dry, flavours not as expected
Small dine-in area

miiniistudio.summary: Tin-box cake specialist on Yanping North Road in Dadaocheng, popular for gift-ready fruit-and-cream cakes in retro tins.
signature: Strawberry tin-box cake (草莓鐵盒蛋糕)
Strawberry cheesecake sandwich cookie (草莓起司蛋糕夾心餅乾)
highlights: Moist honeyed sponge with light Hokkaido cream and big fruit
Beautiful retro tins you can reuse; great for gifts
Friendly in-store pick-up service
lowlights: Pricey (~NT$780 a tin) with a 3-day shelf life
Holiday gift boxes didn't match website photos; arrived early with short expiry
Delivery let some down; pick-up recommended (book ahead)

ningtian.dessert.summary: Small handmade-cake shop centred on crêpe cakes, with whole cakes for birthdays and online same-day slice orders.
highlights: Fruit crêpe packed with fruit; fragrant, not cloying cream
Owner handles feedback well, even replacing a cake
Birthday extras (candles, plates) and birthday-month discount
lowlights: Matcha crêpe called dry with wet, separated cream
Some say only the fruit crêpe is worth it
A bit pricey per cake

icegyaru.summary: Fully vegan Japanese-American soft-serve stand that also sells Okinawan-style onigiri, with weekly rotating flavours.
signature: Oat-milk swirl soft serve (綜合霜淇淋)
Guava + milk-green-tea swirl (芭樂 / 奶綠)
highlights: Vegan food that doesn't taste 'vegan'; hearty onigiri
Cute decor, friendly staff, openly LGBTQ-friendly
Weekly flavour changes; home-delivery packs
lowlights: Order at outside window; only ~3 tables
Long waits (one reviewer queued 1.5h); owner often works solo
Small NT$120 cup, oat-milk taste strong; miso onigiri too salty

tesuan_french_bakery.summary: French baker Ted's sourdough and croissant shop off Dunhua North Road (Songshan), selling out most afternoons.
signature: Blue cheese honey onion focaccia (藍紋蜂蜜洋蔥佛卡夏)
Chestnut walnut country sourdough (鄉村栗子核桃酸種)
Hazelnut almond croissant (榛果杏仁可頌)
highlights: Open, glossy crumb and generous fillings; focaccia a standout
Croissants twice the usual size, denser and slightly sweet
Staff explain each bread; substandard batches are pulled
lowlights: Expensive
Queues; sold out by ~1:30pm
Croissants not the airy, shattering style

tartspace.summary: Takeaway-only tart workshop on Anqing Street, Sanchong, praised for fresh fruit tarts and good value.
signature: Fruit custard cheese tart (水果卡士達乳酪塔)
Earl Grey apple tart (伯爵蘋果塔)
Strawberry Earl Grey chocolate tart (草莓伯爵巧克力塔)
highlights: Crisp, cookie-like crust, not greasy
Fresh, hand-picked fruit; low sweetness
Fair prices and generous ingredients; LINE Pay
lowlights: Slices only Fri–Sun; often sold out by ~2pm
No dine-in, delivery or phone orders; book by DM 2–7 days ahead
Flimsy plastic forks

wujinpatisserie.summary: Tiny financier-and-pudding shop on Zhongshan North Road near the Fine Arts Museum and Expo Park.
signature: Smoked bacon cheese financier (煙燻培根起司費南雪)
Strawberry honey financier (草莓蜂蜜費南雪)
highlights: Bacon-honey financier is a sweet-savoury hit with crisp edges
Silky pudding with bitter caramel and lots of vanilla seeds
Glass window lets you watch the pastry chef
lowlights: Only a handful of reviews so far
Closed Mondays
Small frontage, easy to walk past

gujibakes.summary: Market-born American soft-cookie shop that opened a store near Shuanglian Station (Datong), with a weekly menu.
highlights: Not too sweet for soft cookies; salty-sweet brownie
Rare gluten-free option
Good drinks to pair (hojicha milk, milk tea)
lowlights: Soft-opening hours 12–6pm
Weekly rotating menu; favourites not always on

tasweetokashi.summary: Roll-cake shop back in Taipei on Rui'an Street (Da'an) after years in Luodong, making daily seasonal fruit rolls.
signature: Strawberry Mont Blanc hojicha crisp roll (草莓蒙布朗焙茶脆皮捲)
Mikan mango black tea crisp roll (蜜柑芒果紅茶脆皮捲)
Melon chiffon roll (哈密瓜戚風捲)
highlights: Light Japanese cream, not heavy or cloying
Seasonal and Japanese fruit, made fresh daily
Friendly staff; ice packs for takeaway
lowlights: Fri–Sun afternoons only; sells out early
Very few seats; 60-min limit enforced inconsistently
Pricey; crisp-shell rolls too sweet, soft fillings

frostbite_tw.summary: Ice-cream-cake studio for pick-up in a lane off Xinyi Road near Jinshan South Road (Da'an).
signature: Crunchy caramel ice-cream cake (脆焦糖冰淇淋蛋糕)
Earl Grey Saint-Honoré (伯爵茶聖多諾黑)
highlights: Simple, elegant cakes with clean cross-sections
Layered textures: crisp top, silky cream, cookie base
Chocolate-orange and others not too sweet
lowlights: Melts quickly
Caramel ice cream too sweet for some
Pick-up only; closed Sun–Mon

maisonlevion.summary: Stylish café-pâtisserie in Sanxia, called a hidden gem for its desserts and dirty coffee.
signature: Fleur de sel financier (鹽之花費南雪)
Pistachio Earl Grey dacquoise (開心果伯爵達克瓦茲)
highlights: Crackling caramel top and crisp choux shells
Excellent coffee drinks (dirty, yuzu sparkling americano)
Bright, spacious, pet-friendly space
lowlights: No reservations; queue at 1pm opening, full on weekends
Caramel on the Basque a bit sweet
Some drinks just average

gem.season.summary: Banqiao soft-serve and gelato shop with weekly limited flavours, chestnut Mont Blanc cups and resident cats.
signature: Peach yogurt / pistachio gelato (水蜜桃優格 / 開心果)
Dubai chocolate mochi (杜拜巧克力Q餅)
highlights: Sorbets capture fruit with remarkable depth
New limited flavours almost every week; good value
Seating and friendly shop cats
lowlights: Limited-time flavours are easy to miss
Dubai-chocolate items taste much like others'
Some opt for takeaway when the shop is busy

aufglet_taipei.summary: Taipei branch of a hit Seoul café, with black-minimalist design and brunch dishes as much as bakes.
signature: Maple fried-chicken croffle (楓糖炸雞可朗芙)
Kimchi fried rice with avocado (泡菜炒飯)
Croissant waffle with ice cream (可頌鬆餅)
Grilled vegetable warm salad (碳烤時蔬溫沙拉)
highlights: Sleek, spacious, bright space; pet-friendly
Polite, plentiful staff
Fresh, well-seasoned savoury dishes
lowlights: Desserts and some food called average
Salads too hard and raw for some
Staff watering plants soaked a guest; book ahead

du_pain_sourdough.summary: San Francisco-style sourdough shop near Zhongxiao Fuxing Station exit 2, with generous free tastings.
signature: Tomato garlic sourdough (番茄蒜香酸種)
Jalapeño cheese sourdough (墨西哥辣椒起司)
highlights: Balanced sourness, crisp crust, moist open crumb
Warm staff; tastings with olive oil
Breads pre-sliced, with storage and reheating cards
lowlights: Herbs can overpower; jalapeño mild
No weights on labels; sloppy slicing (~NT$230 per half loaf)
Cash or card only

hamsterdessert.summary: Two-person dessert studio open Fri–Sun, known for matcha cakes and tarts at modest prices.
signature: Matcha pistachio naked cake (抹茶開心果裸蛋糕)
highlights: Authentic, bitter Japanese-style matcha
Cheap cakes and no minimum spend; LINE Pay
Good drinks (taro milk, pearl milk tea)
lowlights: Crêpe cake found dry and stale
Whisked matcha drink watery; flavours flat for some
Few seats; Fri–Sun only, long closures

skiff.tw.summary: Matcha-focused drinks-and-dessert shop on Yanji Street near Sun Yat-sen Memorial Hall Station.
signature: Uji matcha trio (宇治抹茶三重奏)
highlights: Extremely intense matcha; choose your strength
Owner whisks to order and explains how to drink
Thick taro and mung bean desserts
lowlights: Limited dessert bowls (5 a day) can't be reserved
Strong enough to keep you up at night
Hojicha Basque quite powdery

illumine_patisserie.summary: Neighbourhood pâtisserie on Wanquan Street near Shuanglian Station (Datong), known for fruit roll cakes and fruit tarts.
signature: Black tea green grape roll (紅茶綠葡萄蛋糕捲)
Fig fruit tart (無花果水果塔)
Chestnut Mont Blanc cake (栗子蒙布朗)
highlights: Generous, photogenic fruit; consistent quality over many orders
Good value for the quality
Warm, quick staff; fast replies and accepts last-minute orders
lowlights: Only ~6 seats
Cream on the sweet side; sponge can be dry and holey
Table bookings on weekdays only

thenomzie.summary: Soft-cookie café baking thick, chewy cookies daily from 11am, with elegant gift boxes for weddings and holidays.
highlights: Crisp outside, soft inside; reheated warm for dine-in
Fairly low sweetness with layered flavours
Stylish gift packaging; attentive staff
lowlights: Dark chocolate cookie on the sweet side
Coffee only average
Closed Tue–Wed; no reservations

atelier.mho.summary: Small macaron studio (L'Atelier de Mlle HO) taking mainly online orders, praised for Paris-quality macarons.
highlights: Crisp shell, soft centre; rated above big-name brands
Finely balanced spices in seasonal flavours
Beautiful gift boxes; personal touch at pick-up
lowlights: Mainly online pre-orders; DM ahead for in-person purchase
Pick-up paused on some dates
Few reviews; priced at the high end

ponpie.summary: Fruit-tart specialist with a roomy Banqiao café (plus Da'an and mall outlets), known for blueberry and lemon tarts.
signature: Chestnut hojicha pie (栗子烘焙茶派)
highlights: Crisp, fragrant crust; not too sweet
Spacious seating with sockets; laptop-friendly
Friendly staff; good latte and lime coffee
lowlights: Some tarts still too sweet
One-drink minimum, 90-min limit when full; online stock differs
Plastic forks can't cut the crust; parking hard

cheesewithjam_.summary: Quiet, pet-friendly lane café near Jiangzicui known for Basque cheesecakes and custom birthday cakes.
signature: Earl Grey Basque (伯爵茶巴斯克)
Blueberry yogurt Basque (藍莓優格巴斯克)
highlights: Moist, creamy Basques that aren't cloying
Patient custom-cake design with fine details
Calm atmosphere; fair price (NT$880 for 6")
lowlights: No weekend table bookings
Custom cakes ordered via LINE by month
Tucked away in a small lane

crewsdessert.summary: Flight-attendant-themed cake shop with a branch off Dunhua South Road, known for roll cakes and gift boxes.
signature: Normandy cream roll (法國諾曼第生乳捲)
highlights: Light, moist sponge; reduced-sugar recipes
Fun airplane-window seating; cute cutlery
Helpful staff; big range of cakes and cookies
lowlights: Birthday cakes called pricey with a cheap-tasting sponge
Cream texture questioned by some
Cakes can shift in transit

vainabakery.summary: Traditional natural-yeast bakery since 1997 with shops in Tamsui and Beitou, offering a wide range of breads.

Staff slice large loaves; LINE Pay
Baguette gets better the more you chew
lowlights: Bagels soft and Taiwanese-style, little chew
Champion bread bland; some fillings sweet
One complaint about mishandled dropped bread

wuyooo.summary: Small scone café on Tianmu West Road (Shilin), also making pound cakes, cinnamon rolls and breakfast plates.
signature: Apple lemon tea scone (蘋果檸檬茶)
highlights: Dense, very buttery scones in creative flavours
Relaxed space with good music
Good coffee and refillable Oriental Beauty tea
lowlights: Few seats, mostly bar
One report of staff taking tables and splashing guests
Pricey; small drinks; closed Thursdays

daily.needdessert.summary: Linkou dessert shop by a husband-and-wife team, known for cinnamon rolls, Basques and birthday cakes.
signature: Strawberry / mango cream cake (草莓鮮奶油蛋糕)
highlights: Moist cinnamon roll, well-judged sweetness and spice
Light cream; good black coffee; fair prices
Friendly owners; stylish interior
lowlights: Cinnamon rolls sell out by mid-afternoon
Cake order slots fill up
Spare whole cakes only on some days

23_alley_.summary: Tucheng cake shop in a Yusheng Road lane for fruit-cream birthday cakes, shokupan and bagels.

Peach charcoal oolong chantilly (水蜜桃炭焙烏龍)
Strawberry yogurt chantilly (草莓優格香堤)
highlights: Lots of fresh fruit; light, not-sweet cream
Small 4–5" sizes available, even next-day
Strong tea aroma in seasonal cakes
lowlights: No dine-in
Walk-in stock only Fri–Sun; order via LINE
Mid-high price (5" ~NT$980)

18dixhuit_tw.summary: Japanese-style pâtisserie by a Le Cordon Bleu Japan graduate, known for Basques, canelés and ITQI-awarded sablés.

Thai milk tea mochi Basque (泰奶白玉巴斯克)
Caramel fleur de sel latte (焦糖鹽之花拿鐵)
highlights: Canelés crisp outside, soft inside, not too sweet
Quiet, elegant room with big sunny windows
Friendly staff; gift boxes and cheese crackers
lowlights: Taro Basque average; black sesame version sweet
Latte ordinary
Self-bussing; closed Wednesdays

yi.ten_.summary: Custom-cake studio making character cakes with keto, gluten-free and reduced-sugar options.

Gluten-free rice flour and monk-fruit sweetener; not too sweet
Generous, thick cakes; free knife and party kit

Custom designs need lead time

shan3_studio.summary: Tamsui studio now focused on wedding and baby-celebration cookie tins; it no longer sells cakes.
signature: Wedding cookie tins (喜餅鐵盒餅乾)
highlights: Low-sugar, crisp, solid cookies
Cute logo, ribbons and furoshiki wrapping
Stylish Korean-style shop
lowlights: Cakes discontinued; reservation-only via DM
In-store tastings need booking 10 days ahead
Some desserts bland or needing improvement

smile_eating_2.0.summary: One-person, pre-order-only cinnamon-roll maker who also appears at markets.

Still excellent after reheating
Owner treats customers like friends
lowlights: Pre-order only; monthly slots fill quickly
Solo operation, slow message replies
Very few reviews

mi_zhai1004.summary: Animal-themed dessert café near Xindian District Office Station, focused on Taiwanese-tea desserts and icing cookies.

Adorable animal cups and plates; hedgehog decor
Polite staff who advise without upselling
lowlights: One found cookies and coffee average
Scooter parking inconvenient
Many closure days each month

mrmark1998.summary: Health-focused multigrain bakery (Neihu branch) selling wholesome breads, cookies and celebration cakes.

Macadamia multigrain tart (夏威夷豆雜糧塔)
Peanut chocolate cake (花生巧克力蛋糕)

Very warm, helpful staff
Good-value cakes for birthdays and Mother's Day

Tart crust hard, biscuit-style

bread.espresso.and.official.tw.summary: Taipei branch of Tokyo Omotesando's bakery-café near Ximen, famous for Mou toast and brunch French toast.

Mentaiko butter toast (明太子奶油吐司)
highlights: Soft, milky Mou toast; well-plated brunch
Calm Japanese-minimal wooden space
Polite staff, English spoken
lowlights: Pricey; minimum is a main plus a drink
Few small tables; queues, so book or come early
Skimpy ice-cream soda; red bean toast dry

tiaoshi.sourdough.summary: Small Wanhua sourdough and European-bread bakery (Lingo Bakery), mostly pre-order with afternoon opening days.

Pickled chili cheese loaf (剝皮辣椒歐包)

Owner explains her breads passionately

Open only on select afternoons (3–8pm)
Few reviews; whole-wheat loaves dense

oolongcrepes.summary: Japanese-run crêpe shop a minute from Taipei Main Station (exit M6), using Japanese cream and Taiwanese fruit.

Fresh fruit, not too sweet; good value
Calm, clean space; free wifi, refillable tea

Owner's Chinese is limited
Order and pay first

chizupcheesecake.summary: New York-style cheesecake maker known for date-branded 'calendar cakes', with weekday pick-up in Shilin.

Yang Zhi Gan Lu (楊枝甘露)

Fun, photogenic personalised cakes; helpful service

Storage and serving instructions unclear
Pick-up weekdays 1–6pm only

echapper2017.summary: Fresh-cream cake studio with cute hand-painted custom cakes and ready-made small cakes in store.

la_vie_friande.summary: Da'an café, grocery and baking-class studio near the hills, with daily seasonal cakes and homemade dumplings.

maison.stella.summary: Small Wanhua sourdough bakery on a Qingnian Road lane using Taiwanese wheat; open Wed–Sat afternoons.

Local Taiwanese wheat and cocoa

Wed–Sat only (Saturday the only weekend day)
Some loaves bland or powdery

pf.pastrydesign.summary: Elegant French pâtisserie beside Fuzhou railway station with a piano lounge upstairs, also making Viennoiserie.

orita.japancakes.summary: Japanese-owned cake shop since 2016 in a lane near Zhongxiao Fuxing, known for fruit crêpe cakes and chiffons.

taipeileechi.summary: Taipei Leechi's only store, a century-old traditional pastry house for pineapple cakes and Mid-Autumn mooncakes.

weekendnodessert.summary: Order-only birthday-cake studio (no custom designs) with pick-up from a private studio near Zhongshan Station.

chun.pain.summary: Xizhi bakery using house levain and natural ingredients, with breads from around the world, cakes and classes.

Croissant gelato weekends only (NT$230)
Greek yogurt on the sweet side
